title: You Think Cold Logic Makes Wise Choices, Yet Losing Emotion Paralyses Decisions

acts.name: Pure Logic Myth & Patient Elliot's 130-IQ Paralysis
sentences: You were taught that smart choices need cold logic!
Yet patients who lose emotion cannot even pick a lunch spot!
This is the true story of Antonio Damasio's Iowa Gambling Task.
Here is what went wrong with the myth of cold logic.
In Iowa, doctors treated Elliot after tumor surgery.
Surgery hurt his ventromedial prefrontal cortex, the judgment center behind the eyes.
Elliot kept a one hundred thirty IQ, like a computer!
He passed every logic test in the clinic.
Yet picking a date took thirty minutes, like a lunch break — and that wasn't the strangest part.

acts.name: 1994 Iowa Gambling Task: Decks A/B ($1,250 Loss) vs C/D
sentences: Why would a genius ruin his life and savings?
In nineteen ninety-four, the Iowa team built a card game.
Players flipped one hundred cards from four decks: A, B, C, and D.
Decks A and B paid one hundred dollars, like a jackpot!
Yet hidden inside were huge two hundred fifty dollar traps!
Decks C and D paid fifty dollars with tiny penalties.
Healthy players soon avoided the dangerous A and B decks.
Frontal patients kept drawing from trap decks until bankrupt!
Watching a genius walk into ruin was a total nightmare.

acts.name: 1997 Skin-Conductance Discovery: Your Palms Know by Card 10
sentences: Why did patients with intact math fall for bad decks?
In nineteen ninety-seven, the team wired sensors onto palms.
Whenever a hand hovered, sensors tracked sweat.
Healthy people did not state the rule until card eighty.
Yet by card ten, like ten flips, palms sweated over the risky deck!
Forty-five cards before hunches, the body sounded an alarm!
The team called that warning a somatic marker.
Your insula, the gut-feeling center, and amygdala, your alarm, tag choices!
But here's the twist: what showed up on the patients' sensors?

acts.name: Card 50 Conscious Hunch vs Card 80 Explicit Rule — Yet Patients Still Lose
sentences: Frontal patients showed zero sweat before picking bad cards!
By card eighty, half the patients knew the rule!
They pointed at decks A and B and called them traps.
Then their hands reached back to the risky deck!
Without a gut alarm from the ventromedial prefrontal cortex, risk feels weightless!
Pure logic lists pros and cons but never decides.
Emotion is not the enemy of reason.
Instead of clouding judgment, emotion is the compass that steers reason!

acts.name: 2005 Shiv Investment Paradox: When Zero Fear Beats Healthy Traders
sentences: Do gut feelings always win in every game?
In two thousand five, a new team flipped that test!
He gave players twenty rounds of a coin game.
Logically, you should invest every round for returns.
After losing a round, healthy players held back!
Fearless patients invested eighty percent of rounds and earned more!
The researchers were left completely stunned.
Gut feelings save you from traps, yet overreact to streaks.

acts.name: When to Trust vs Override Your Gut & Viewer Takeaway
sentences: How do you know when to trust your gut today?
Your insula, the gut-feeling center, learns patterns from experience.
In familiar tasks, a knot in your stomach is real data!
Never ignore that warning when a deal looks shiny.
Yet after a random loss, check if fear makes you timid.
Pair your body's alarm with your brain's math.
Wise choices need both a compass and a map.
Which proves you cannot think clearly without feeling, because your body warns you first.
